principles.text: There's no correct trim-vs-hold answer; if unsure, toss a coin, then review the closed trade later to gradually build your own selling style. Trimming an extended (far from 9 EMA) name helps you stay on the boat through a potential ~20% pullback.

Buying pullbacks: prefer the entry where price just lists a little sideways at support; use a lower-timeframe EMA (e.g. 60-min 9 EMA) as the reference/trigger and pick whichever timeframe works best for you.

The lowest spot at support is the best risk/reward pullback entry, but it's hard to catch — strong stocks 'touch and go' at support; if a stock starts chopping around the 21 EMA for several days it's an early sign of losing strength.
A gap-up is generally a lower-probability time to buy new positions (expect more fade), but it's a tendency, not a black-and-white rule to avoid all entries; gap-downs into support are better timing.

Be open-minded and curious: don't blindly follow any concept or trader; think twice about new ideas, keep the good ones, discard the bad, and form your own style. Curiosity drives finding good risk/reward entries by studying past moves.

Your opinions on where a random stock 'will go' are useless and unimportant; ask actionable questions (was X a good entry/exit at a specific level/timeframe) rather than 'what do you think of ticker Y'.
